item.title: 'Killed her, then went to sleep': Chilling calm of nurse killer baffles cops
item.description: A bike mechanic was arrested for raping and strangling a nurse in Pahadishareef. He allegedly watched the woman for a month before entering her room through a window. The accused returned to his garage and slept after committing the crime. Mobile data and forensic evidence helped investigators crack the difficult case. Police are checking the accused's criminal record in Bihar.

item.title: Pakistan chaos: PCB seeks answers over Rizwan, Imam picks as Misbah quits committee
item.description: Pakistan Cricket Board seeks explanation from its selection committee. The board questioned the rationale behind including Mohammad Rizwan and Imam-ul-Haq. This action follows the team's poor performance in the ongoing England Test series. Several players and coaching staff have been released and replaced amid this overhaul. Misbah-ul-Haq is reportedly set to resign from the selection committee.

item.title: Oracle layoffs: The 6 am email didn't come, so employees are counting Slack members
item.description: Oracle layoffs 2026: The dreaded 6 am layoff email did not arrive on September 1, leaving employees across the US and India tracking Slack member counts and trading rumours of a September 15 date. Managers were asked to list affected staff before Oracle's second fiscal quarter began. After 21,000 job cuts, $55.7 billion in AI data centre spending and $1.8 billion in restructuring charges, Oracle staff are still waiting.

item.title: NASA sent 3,301 bees into space in 1984 to study honeycomb without gravity
item.description: In a groundbreaking 1984 mission aboard NASA's Space Shuttle Discovery, thousands of honeybees ventured into space. They showcased remarkable adaptability by constructing around 200 cm of honeycomb in microgravity. Researchers noted variations in the size and structure of the cells, diverging from typical Earth patterns. This experiment sought to unravel how bees organize in the absence of gravity, revealing that behavior is crucial for their collaboration.

item.title: Florida couple preserved 1908 home for 41 years; now it is a historic landmark
item.description: In Oneco, Florida, the Johnson Helm House has earned the title of the first local historic landmark in the county. Built in 1908, this charming residence has been lovingly preserved by Margi and Pat Nanney for over four decades, keeping its unique architectural attributes intact. Their commitment has prevented modern alterations from obscuring its character, while this recognition emphasizes the area's important agricultural history.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: New Jersey woman paid $40,000 for land; town now wants it for 340 homes
item.description: A woman from South Jersey has taken a stand against the government's plan to acquire her land, which is intended for a new housing development in Middle Township. She asserts that the seizure does not serve public interest. Ongoing legal proceedings and negotiations haven't resolved the matter, underscoring the potential consequences of eminent domain on marginalized communities.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Mark Zuckerberg buys 440-acre Irish castle estate; spokesperson says family is ‘excited’
item.description: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan have acquired the impressive Strancally Castle, a historic estate sprawling over 440 acres in County Waterford, Ireland. They intend to use this majestic castle as a residence during their trips to Ireland, reinforcing Meta's strong ties to the country where its international headquarters are situated.

item.title: Nepal floods bring 'unusual' fish to Bihar, govt warns people not to eat or sell them
item.description: In light of recent floods from Nepal, the Bihar government has issued a warning about the presence of strange fish species in the Gandak river. Residents are advised to avoid consuming or selling these unidentified fish until their safety can be verified. Among these is the goonch catfish, locally called Gochita. Anyone who falls ill after eating these fish is urged to seek medical assistance promptly.
item.dc:creator: DILIP KUMAR

item.title: Vice-captain Sooryavanshi shines as East beat Central to reach Duleep Trophy final
item.description: East Zone secured a place in the Duleep Trophy final with a four-wicket victory over Central Zone. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's aggressive cameo provided crucial momentum during the chase for East Zone. Mohammed Shami and Mukesh Kumar delivered fiery spells to dismantle Central Zone's batting lineup. Mukesh was named Player of the Match for his outstanding seven-wicket haul in the semifinal.

item.title: Maharashtra puts FDA action against loose edible oil sales on hold for 1 year
item.description: Maharashtra's chief minister has deferred enforcement action on loose edible oil sales for one year. Traders must comply with the law after this mandatory transition period ends. Joint committees will guide traditional traders in making necessary business practice changes. The government will assist businesses with facilities and potential subsidies for compliance. This decision balances public health concerns with the livelihoods of many traders.
item.dc:creator: SIDDHI DHARMADHIKARI

item.title: Operation ‘Rotten Apple’: US arrests over 2,100 illegal immigrants across New York
item.description: During a comprehensive operation aimed at reinforcing public safety, US Immigration and Customs Enforcement detained 2,197 undocumented individuals throughout New York. Many of those arrested had serious criminal records. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin emphasized that the operation was crucial for enhancing safety in the state while criticizing local officials for their lack of cooperation with federal agencies.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: India's GDP grows 7.8% in Q1: Factors powering the economy despite global turmoil
item.description: In the first quarter, India showcased impressive economic resilience with a remarkable 7.8% GDP growth. The surge was notably driven by a surge in domestic demand and the services sector. Additionally, investment activity picked up pace, enhancing the overall economic landscape. This achievement stands out amid global geopolitical tensions and market fluctuations, reinforcing India's status as the fastest-growing major economy in the world.
item.dc:creator: SHIVANGHI PAYAL

item.title: Crumbling 1979 Michigan dome bought for $87,000 now lists for $499,900
item.description: In Brighton, Michigan, a remarkable transformation has taken place with a once-neglected 1970s concrete dome home. Acquired in 2023 for $87,000, this property underwent a meticulous renovation, now boasting four bedrooms infused with modern luxury and eco-friendly features. Now on the market for $499,900, its unique design and energy-efficient qualities are captivating buyers in search of distinctive living spaces.

item.title: Emma Jarman met Dolly Parton as a newborn; 18 years later, she shares the story
item.description: Eighteen-year-old Emma Jarman recalls meeting Dolly Parton when she was just one day old at Rotherham Hospital in 2007. The singer had visited the UK to launch her Imagination Library literacy initiative, with Emma becoming its first UK recipient. Emma now reflects on their surreal encounter and Parton’s lasting impact on her life.

item.description: Over time, the interest earned on the accumulated balance earns interest, allowing compounding to steadily increase your retirement savings. With regular contributions maintained over a long period, an employee can potentially build an EPF corpus of Rs 1 crore or more.

item.title: ‘Hope is still alive’: Krunal reacts after missing out on India’s Afghan T20I squad
item.description: Krunal Pandya remains optimistic about his potential return to international cricket after his absence in the Afghanistan T20I series. Jasprit Bumrah is set to rejoin the team, contingent on a positive fitness assessment concerning his knee injury. Additionally, several players, including Nitish Kumar Reddy, are included pending their fitness. Hardik Pandya, however, will not participate due to a leg issue affecting his comeback strategy.

item.title: Asian Games cricket row: Japan Cricket CEO says teams can make own arrangements
item.description: Japan Cricket CEO Naoki Alex Miyaji clarified Asian Games accommodation arrangements for teams. Participating teams are offered hotel stays and can arrange their own lodging. Logistical constraints are affecting many sports, not just cricket at the event. The Korogi Sports Park venue was built from scratch within a tight timeframe. Organisers are confident cricket will make a strong impression at the Games.

item.title: MPSC exam paper leak: ‘Top ranker’ arrested, intentionally gave 10 wrong answers
item.description: Mumbai Police arrested a top-ranking MPSC candidate in the drug inspector exam leak case. This arrest brings the total number of accused individuals to seven now. Police allege the candidate received the leaked paper and answered questions incorrectly. The MPSC had previously cancelled the recruitment process due to the alleged breach. A fresh examination will now be conducted to ensure fairness for all.

item.title: Polish priest survived Nazi malaria experiments, then built Nebraska shrine
item.description: Father Henry J. Denis emerged from the horrors of Dachau concentration camp and the inhumane medical experiments conducted there. With a steadfast vow to create a shrine to Mary if he survived, he eventually settled in Nebraska, where he honored that promise. The Our Lady of Fatima Shrine, dedicated in August 1956, serves as a powerful symbol of hope and unwavering faith transcending time and geography.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Boston teen, 19, dies after jumping onto train tracks to save girlfriend
item.description: A nineteen-year-old man lost his life in a tragic act of courage while on his first subway journey. He leaped onto the tracks after his girlfriend stumbled, attempting to save her. Unfortunately, he came into contact with the electric third rail. Now in critical condition, his girlfriend is hospitalized, spurring urgent calls for better safety measures on subway platforms.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: ‘May land me in hot water’: Multan Sultans CEO delivers explosive take on Pak cricket
item.description: Pakistan Cricket Board's recent squad and coaching changes have drawn significant criticism. Multan Sultans CEO Gohar Shah voiced concerns over player professionalism and team intensity. He also highlighted issues within the wider cricket ecosystem, including media and former players. Shah pointed to bureaucratic hurdles and a lack of incentive for PCB stakeholders. His assessment offered a candid view on the state of Pakistan cricket.
item.dc:creator: HIJAM RAJU SINGH

item.title: Pankaj Bhadouria shares ‘Cancer’ changed her; says 'Was weakened by infections'
item.description: MasterChef India champion Pankaj Bhadouria has bravely opened up about her ongoing battle with breast cancer. Faced with serious health challenges this August, including painful infections and the emotional toll of hair loss, she has leaned on the love of family and friends. A recent outing with her loved ones symbolizes her resilience and progress, as Pankaj continues to embrace life with optimism and support despite the circumstances.
item.dc:creator: etimes.in

item.title: Kerala Teen's Viral Resemblance: Allen James dubbed Kerala's Yamal; hopes for Yamal message
item.description: A teenager from Kerala, Allen James, has captured the internet's attention with his remarkable likeness to football player Lamine Yamal. A video showcasing his talent has gone viral, racking up millions of views across various social media sites. As a defender with a passion for football, Allen idolizes Lionel Messi and proudly supports Argentina.

item.title: UPI gets festive boost: Digital payments hit a record 24.51 bn transactions in August
item.description: In August, Unified Payments Interface hit an all-time high for monthly transaction volumes, largely fueled by festive celebrations like Raksha Bandhan that encouraged peer-to-peer transfers. As transaction values approached previous peaks, the digital payment landscape continued to evolve, with UPI now being embraced in eleven countries worldwide. The potential for further growth is promising as innovative use cases, such as credit options within UPI, start to gain traction.
